answer: Call POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profile (singular = one profile; POST /api/profiles takes {"profiles": [...]} for many). Not api.identitynow.com and not /non-employee-records (that is ISC NELM). Header Authorization: Bearer <ISC JWT> with scope nerm:api:profile-manager, nerm:api:integration-partner (create only) or nerm:general:manage. The body must be wrapped: {"profile": {"name": "Jane Doe", "profile_type_id": "<uuid of the Non-Employees profile type from GET /api/profile_types>", "status": "Active", "attributes": {"personal_first_name": "Jane", "personal_last_name": "Doe", "start_date": "01/15/2026", "organization": "<org profile id>"}}}. profile_type_id (an id, not a name) and status (Active, Inactive, On Leave, Terminated) are required. attributes are keyed by attribute uid (not label); text = string, profile/user select = target id (array if multi), dates in the attribute's date_format. Response: {"profile": {...}} with the new id. Sending the bare object is the classic 400; validation errors come as {"error":..., "errors": {"attr": "can't be blank"}}. Validate the body offline with scripts/check_nerm.py body.json.

Yes, and that is now the recommended way. Create a personal access token (client id + secret) in ISC, exchange it with POST https://{isc-tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token using grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, then send the returned access_token (a JWT) to NERM as Authorization: Bearer <JWT> on https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/.... The token carries the access of the ISC user who made the PAT and needs at least one nerm: scope (nerm:general:manage, nerm:api:read-only, nerm:api:profile-manager, etc.); it expires (expires_in, about 12.5 minutes in the guide's example), so refresh it. The PAT itself is not sent to NERM, only the JWT. Legacy NERM API keys (NERM Admin > System > Api) still exist but are deprecated, have no scopes, cannot be used by tenants created after June 2025 or by FedRAMP customers, and are not described in the OpenAPI security scheme.

Use nerm:api:workflow-operator. It gives read on profiles, profile types, workflows and advanced search, plus read and execute of workflow sessions, which is exactly 'start sessions and read profiles'. It is the only scope besides nerm:general:manage that can execute workflow sessions; nerm:api:profile-reader or nerm:api:read-only can read profiles but cannot run POST /workflow_sessions?run=true, and nerm:general:manage gives everything including system configuration (too much). Scopes only exist on ISC tokens (PAT exchanged at /oauth/token); legacy NERM API keys have no scopes. If a scope is missing, NERM returns 403 with a generic body {"error": "You do not have the permission to access this resource."} that never names the missing scope, so check the token's scopes first (scripts/check_nerm.py --scopes nerm:api:workflow-operator --request "POST /workflow_sessions" confirms the call is allowed).

Use keyset paging with after_id, not offset. GET https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profiles?limit=500&metadata=true (500 is the max on /profiles, default 100), then repeat with &after_id=<last id returned, or _metadata.after_id/next> until a page returns fewer than limit (or empty). after_id forces sorting by id ascending and cannot be combined with offset; other filters are ignored or rejected with 400 except profile_type_id and limit (so no status, name, archived alongside it). For a nightly delta, add updated_after=YYYY-MM-DD, which may be combined with after_id. Add exclude_attributes=true only if you don't need attribute values. Responses are {"profiles": [...], "_metadata": {limit, total, next, after_id}}. Don't use ISC-style count/sorters/filters parameters. No rate limits are documented, but back off on 429 and refresh the ISC JWT (expires about every 12 minutes) during a long run. ~200,000 profiles = about 400 calls.

Because POST /workflow_sessions does not start the workflow unless you add the query parameter run=true (default false). Without it you get a session in status new that just sits there. Either create with POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/workflow_sessions?run=true, or start the existing one with PATCH /api/workflow_sessions/{id}?run=true. Body must be wrapped: {"workflow_session": {"workflow_id": "<id>", "requester_id": "<user id>", "requester_type": "User", "profile_id": "<for update workflows>", "attributes": {...prefill by attribute uid}}}; workflow_id, requester_id and requester_type (User, NeprofileUser, NeaccessUser, NeaccessRegistrant) are required, profile_ids for batch workflows. Executing needs scope nerm:api:workflow-operator or nerm:general:manage (otherwise a generic 403). If it does run but stops later, look at status (pending_approval waits for an approver; failed can be a REST API step over 60 s) or a Close Session step. scripts/check_nerm.py flags sessions that will not start.

Use advanced search; there is no filters= expression on /profiles. First get the id of the first-name attribute (uid personal_first_name) with GET https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/ne_attributes (the rule needs the attribute id). Then POST /api/advanced_search/run?limit=500&offset=0 with {"advanced_search": {"condition_rules_attributes": [{"type": "ProfileStatusRule", "comparison_operator": "!=", "value": "Terminated"}, {"type": "ProfileAttributeRule", "condition_object_type": "TextFieldAttribute", "condition_object_id": "<attribute id>", "comparison_operator": "start_with?", "value": "a"}]}}. All rules must match (AND). The spec uses condition_object_type = the attribute's type; the guide's examples use "object_type": "NeAttribute" (check_nerm.py accepts both and warns). The response is {"profiles": [...]}; page with limit/offset. Add a ProfileTypeRule (== profile type id) to restrict to non-employees. To reuse it, save with POST /advanced_search and run with GET /advanced_search/{id}/run. Needs a scope that reads advanced search (profile-reader, profile-manager, workflow-operator, read-only).

They are different products. NERM (Non-Employee Risk Management, formerly SecZetta) is a separate SaaS add-on at https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com with its own API (/api/profiles, /api/workflow_sessions...). It models any number of profile types (people, organizations, jobs, assignments, assets) with custom attributes and relationships, has configurable lifecycle workflows (create, update, batch, automated) and collaboration workflows for an external portal (registration, login, password reset) with 25+ action types, and per-attribute risk scoring. Non-Employee Lifecycle Management (NELM) is a feature inside ISC itself: non-employee sources with their own schema and records, a simple request/approval flow by account managers, no risk scoring, and its API on https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com (/non-employee-sources, /non-employee-records, /non-employee-requests, /non-employee-approvals). SailPoint positions NELM as the basic option and NERM for automation, self-service onboarding, delegated administration and external portals. NERM can feed ISC: person profiles become identities through the NERM connector, and ISC PATs authenticate to the NERM API.

Risk scoring is off by default and enabled per profile type, on a 0-10 scale with default levels Low/Medium/High (/risk_levels). Only option-based attributes can carry risk: drop-down, check boxes, radio buttons, profile search and profile select (text, date etc. cannot). Each attribute gets a risk type: Impact, Probability, Impact and Probability, Inherited (only profile search/select: takes the linked profile's risk) or None, with values per option; mitigation attributes can lower an attribute's risk. Overall score = average of (average impact score, average probability score), rounded to two decimals. If an inherited (linked) profile has a higher score, it overrides and raises the profile's score. Subcategories are displayed but do not change the score. Via API: GET /api/risk_scores returns objects of type Profile or WorkflowSession with overall, impact and probability scores and level ids; advanced search can filter with a RiskRule (secondary_value OverallRisk, operators ==, >, <).

The SailPoint Non-Employee Risk Management connector aggregates profiles as accounts. Non-Employee Profile ID is aggregated automatically and mapped to Employee Number; default correlation is Non-Employee Profile ID = Employee Number (changing it can create duplicate identities). First Name, Last Name and Business Email are required core attributes. Only person profile types (core Non-Employees, custom employee/non-employee categories, plus assignments as additional accounts correlated through their profile search/select attribute) are synced; enable it per type in NERM Admin > System > Identity Security Cloud Connection Settings (NON-EMPLOYEE / ASSIGNMENT tab). The source status filter is All or Active (Active + On Leave); archived profiles are never aggregated. Not all attributes sync: only those in the account schema (all strings), extended attributes do not sync, and entitlement aggregation is not supported for profile sources. Make only person profiles authoritative. API side: /api/isc/accounts and /api/profile_types/{id}/synced_attributes. NERM users and roles go through the separate NERM Users connector (matched on sailpoint_identity_id).

Yes, two. Status Change applies immediately when the step runs: placed before the approval, the profile is set to Terminated even if the manager later rejects. Move Status Change after the approval step. The REST API step times out after 60 seconds and the workflow session then fails, so a slow service will break the run; make the call fast (have the service accept and process asynchronously) or move the slow work outside NERM. Also remember automated workflows have no button: they run once a day at a fixed time set by the tenant's AWS region (not changeable), and select profiles with filters that must all match (e.g. end date reached), so an approval step means the session waits in pending_approval until the manager acts. A Close Session step ends the workflow and nothing after it runs.
